# s248 — refs must not let a later reference borrow an earlier reference's anchor

On a line such as "`Box` (`src/app.py:1`) and `src/app.py:9` later", `slicer refs` anchors both references to `Box`. The second one was never anchored by its author, yet `--fix` rewrites it. An anchor should belong to the first reference after it, and to no other. <!-- example -->

**Findings:** s246 reviewer probe, 2026-10-11: `Box` (`src/app.py:1`) and `src/app.py:9` rewrote :9 to :3 · **Size:** S · **Trees:** src/slicer, tests, docs

**2026-10-11** — s249 relay: the Why examples are marked. The lead's example refs (src/app.py lines 1 and 9) wait for s252 (edit --lead); mark them with that flag once it lands.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** other anchor rules (qualified names, common-word anchors); the range rule (s246); any change to which text refs scans.

## Why

Found by the s246 reviewer (2026-10-11): the probe rewrote `src/app.py:9` to `:3`. That follows the owner's rule, "the nearest backticked identifier before it on the same line". But the rule did not consider two references sharing one line, so an unanchored reference gets silently rewritten. The real roadmap shows the same pattern. S133 anchors four files to `_census`, and S148 anchors `docs/agents.md:271` to `_strict_flag`. <!-- example -->

## Files

- `src/slicer/refs.py`, in `find`: an anchor is consumed by the first reference that follows it. A later reference on the same line with no backticked identifier between the two is `unanchored`.
- `tests/test_refs.py`.
- `docs/commands.md`, if it states the anchor rule. `CHANGELOG.md`.
